model.name: M3t
model.note: the assignment rule is world-FAMILY knowledge (I wrote the generator), not a blind inference; A06 utilisation only confirmed it is consistent

predictions.experiment: OBS-005..012: eight fresh world runs, lambda=1.6, c=4, horizon 6000, warmup 300, run-seeds 101..108, level 3
predictions.claim: the mean of W_mean over the eight runs falls in [2.891, 3.109] (M3t predictive 95% interval for an 8-run mean; point 2.996)
predictions.if_it_fails: M3t is mis-specified for the waiting-time law at moderate load; the OBS-003 excess was not luck and a further mechanism is needed
predictions.if_it_holds: the OBS-003 miss was ordinary run-to-run variation and M3t stands

predictions.experiment: OBS-013: lambda=2.0, c=6, horizon 6000, warmup 300, run-seed 21, level 3
predictions.claim: servers 0,1,2,3 reproduce the pool rates 0.6930 / 0.3625 / 0.3625 / 1.0275 within their 95% CIs; servers 4 and 5 have stable, server-specific, exponential service (per-server CV in [0.92, 1.08]).
predictions.declared_unknown: the RATES of servers 4 and 5. Four observed rates are not enough to identify the distribution they are drawn from, so the model cannot predict capacity at c>4. This is a boundary of M3t, stated before the observation rather than after it.
predictions.if_it_fails: server identity is not a persistent property and the pool abstraction must be replaced
